title: Alpha Trader
content: believes, they can ever burn out people have experienced almost exclusively success in their early life. Can't imagine ever being tired or burnt out or failing, but trading is exhausting. If you don't manage your stress level properly and stay somewhat healthy in your 20s and 30s. You Probably won't be trading in your 40s or 50s. 1 Trader. I work with had her Apple watch monitoring or heart rate as the FED announced its interest rate decision in August 2019 she had a ton of orders to watch and was at significant risk through the meeting. In the PDF, there's a chart of her heart rate as it goes from 60, beats per minute, resting to 100 beats per minute on the FED announcement. It's a cool chart. Here's how good Traders deal with stress. First have perspective, like I said earlier we're not storming, the beaches of Normandy here, we're buying and selling Assets in an attempt to generate short-term profits. If you can take the job seriously and treat it as a profession, but still understand the sun will come up tomorrow no matter how well or badly you trade you can win. Next. Relax, learn to relax and breathe. When you have big risk on, don't wait knuckle every trade and grind your teeth over every basis point jiggle. You need to get come. Comfortable with being uncomfortable. This took me a long time but it's a nice State of Mind to have a ton of risk on and know that you can see the world clearly and breathe. This does not mean you don't care. It just means you put on risk before you'll put on risk again and this is just a single trial in a process with thousands of Trials, each trade is a spoonful of water in an ocean. Don't get riled up. Third. Go off the desk, many Traders, hate to go off the desk because they're worried about missing something. In the long, run, the benefits you gain from. Going off the desk, exceed the risk you take of missing something. When you go off the desk, your heart rate goes down. And you'll often experience, stunning moments of clarity. Every experienced Trader knows the feeling of that super clear Market Insight, that pops into your head when you're off the desk. The human brain produces new ideas by creating connections between disparate thoughts and stimuli and it does this best when it is at rest to achieve Clarity and produce aha moments. Of trading Insight, sometimes you need to go off the desk and let your brain work. Much in the way. Sleep allows your brain to process everything, you've experienced. During the day, pulling yourself away from the screens allows your brain to cool off and run some different less urgent sub routines. Frequently heard on the trading floor, man. I just realized something really interesting on my way back from the bathroom. The next tip for long-term survival and stress reduction is turn off your phone at night. Checking your phone for 4 times, a night makes you feel important. And allows you to impress, your friends with your aggressive commitment to Capital markets. Checking your phone at night is more addiction than useful habit. Markets are always awake but you need time to rest. They'll be fine with you for a few hours. Leave a stop-loss and a take profit on every position you hold at night, then, turn off your phone and get some proper sleep. I used to leave call levels in various currencies, and I get the call from Hong Kong or Tokyo, or London. At 2:30 a.m. this would result in wife annoyed young kids awake, no good trade since I had no idea what was going on in the market and was groggy and not in a strong position to make split-second decisions and much more tired. The next day because of elevated heart rate in the middle of the night and 60 Minutes of tossing, and turning and half awake dreams about Delian before finally falling asleep, 20 minutes before my alarm went off in the morning. Eventually, I left instructions with all the other Centers, do not call me at night still even once I kick the call level have it. If I woke up to go to the bathroom, in the middle of the night, I was always tempted to check the market. Again, this is pointless, do not do it. Turn your phone off. When you go to bed, turn it back on when you wake up. Took me many years to learn this and implemented and my health and Sleep Quality improved dramatically when I did. Well, rested, outperformed sleep deprived. It is common sense, but research also shows conclusively. That humans perform tasks at a substantially higher level when properly rested and we make persistent and frequent errors. When sleep-deprived And finally, breathe. Learn how to focus on your breath through meditation yoga or other mindfulness practices. The ability to deal with stress is somewhat innate. But you can learn Stress Management and be thoughtful about your own reaction to pressure. Again, try to step outside yourself at times and make observations, hmm. I just smashed my fist on the keyboard. Maybe I should take a little walk, observe your own behavior and understand what it might mean. I have a huge lump in my throat and I want to yell this trade is getting under my skin in a bad way. I need to square up and start fresh tomorrow. The struggle for self-awareness is a Timeless piece of The Human Condition. Greater self-awareness will help you in trading and will help you in real life. Now, let's move on to the next non-cognitive trait on our list. Focus. Alpha Traders maintain Focus, even when flaming arrows are raining down on the battlefield and everyone else is losing their mind. Trading floors are quieter
